title: publish-release.sh hashes the root launcher tarball up to ~30 min before npm publish reads it
description: Found by the reviewer pass on opum-ai/lore-cli#269 (LCLI-578), finding 6, PLAUSIBLE, not reproduced. The receipt gate hashes every tarball in $ARTIFACTS once, before any publish. The root launcher is published last, only after the registry-visibility wait (REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS, default 1800 s) plus a 20 s cushion. Nothing in the script writes to $ARTIFACTS in that window (the README gate uses tar -xzOf, read-only), so only an outside process could swap the file. That is a narrow TOCTOU between the digest check and the bytes npm reads. Options: publish from a private read-only copy made at check time, or re-hash the root tarball immediately before its npm publish and refuse on drift.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The root launcher tarball handed to npm publish is proven byte-identical to the one the receipt gate hashed, by a copy made at check time or a re-hash immediately before publish
A test swaps the root tarball after the gate and before its publish, and the script refuses before publishing it

plan: Keep the receipt the LCLI-578 gate read (script-level path, cleaned on EXIT via the existing trap pattern) instead of deleting it

In publish_one, immediately before npm publish (and before the dry-run would-publish line), re-hash the tarball with shasum -a 256 and compare with the receipt tarballs[<file>] (own-property node -e lookup); die before publishing on mismatch or unreadable value
Correct the ROOT LAUNCHER provenance prose in scripts/publish-release.sh header and docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md
Tests in test/publish-release-script.test.ts: root swap, later-platform swap (and dry-run if hookable); mutation-test the re-hash
implementationNotes: Also in scope when this lands (from LCLI-568, 2026-09-25): scripts/publish-release.sh:77-79 and docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md:696 still say the root launcher's sha256 is 'recorded nowhere' and 'irreducibly a LOCAL SELF-SEAL'. Since LCLI-578 (#269), the qualification receipt from opum-cli-e2e records it and the gate refuses on mismatch, which I measured live on 0.9.3 with a re-gzipped root. Correct both to say what now binds the root launcher, and what still does not (the check-to-publish window this task is about).
Context pack (lore agent context implementation) omitted runbooks/release-publishing and scripts/publish-release.sh; both are named by the task, so read directly.

Also refused on real 0.9.3 bytes: dry-run with the re-gzipped real root swapped at the root own pre-publish npm view -> exit 1, receipt c70fd8db... vs e31ccb0c.... finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#275. The pre-publish window is closed: scripts/publish-release.sh keeps the qualification receipt the LCLI-578 gate read (RECEIPT_FILE; one cleanup_private_files EXIT/INT/TERM trap removes it and the private npmrc). publish_one calls recheck_against_receipt as its last step before npm publish, and before a --dry-run would-publish line. It re-hashes with shasum -a 256 and compares with the receipt tarballs[<file>] (own-property lookup). A mismatch or an unreadable value dies before publishing, naming the file and both digests. This covers all seven packages; --verify-only is untouched. The root-launcher provenance prose in the script header and docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md now says the receipt binds the root. opum-cli-e2e re-hashes that digest from the same Release run npm-packages artifact, so it is recorded by another repository but is not a second, independent build. rootTarballSha256 stays unused (zlib-dependent, LCLI-568). Tests 45 -> 51: positive control, root swap, later-platform swap, dry-run swap, and an unreadable receipt value (real reader and silent reader). Mutation-tested M1-M4, each matching its predicted subset. Real 0.9.3 artifacts (Release run 36088480940), with an npm shim answering view as absent: 7/7 rehash lines pass; a re-gzipped real root swapped after the gate is refused (c70fd8db... vs e31ccb0c...). Evidence is in the notes. Needs a reviewer pass before landing (scripts/).
